turns.content: Good morning, everyone. I'm Alex Chen, Chief Procurement Officer. Let's start by confirming our roles: Mr. Wang will lead the commercial side, Emma Liu will cover quality and operations, and Manager Zhang will support us with market benchmarks. Our agenda is to discuss unit price, delivery lead time, and the joint quality inspection protocol, aiming for a mutually acceptable agreement. I’ll begin by outlining our target: unit price ≤ 85 RMB, delivery within 30 days, and an accepted quality protocol. I invite Mr. Wang to share the supplier’s initial proposal.

Thank you, Alex. Our initial commercial proposal is a unit price of 84 RMB and a standard delivery lead time of 28 days. We are prepared to work with you on a joint quality inspection protocol and would appreciate a reliable annual volume commitment to ensure sustainable margins.

For reference, the current market benchmark for this component is 83 RMB per unit. Your target of ≤ 85 RMB is therefore aligned with market levels, giving us a solid baseline for the price discussion.

Thank you, Mr. Wang. Your price of 84 RMB and 28‑day lead time meet our target thresholds. To move forward, could you confirm the annual volume you anticipate committing to? Emma, could you outline the key steps and responsibilities for the joint quality inspection protocol you envision, so we can ensure alignment with our standards. Manager Zhang, please have any benchmark data on comparable inspection practices ready for reference.

Based on our production capacity and forecast, we can comfortably commit to an annual volume of 100,000 units, provided the price remains at 84 RMB and the delivery terms stay at 28 days. This volume would give us the scale needed to maintain a sustainable margin while ensuring supply stability for your program.

Our joint quality inspection protocol would include: 1) Pre‑production sample approval with both parties present; 2) Incoming material inspection on receipt; 3) In‑process QC checkpoints at key production stages; 4) Final product inspection by a joint audit team before shipment; 5) Detailed inspection reports and agreed corrective‑action procedures. To ensure we can meet the 28‑day lead time without compromising quality, we need evidence of your production capacity and any risk mitigations you have in place.

Industry data shows a typical joint inspection protocol: a first‑piece audit covering the first 5 % of output, then random sampling of about 2 % of each batch, with results reported within 2 business days. The associated cost overhead averages 1‑2 % of unit price. Your 84 RMB offer is just 1 RMB above the market benchmark (83 RMB), which is acceptable provided the volume commitment supports supplier margin.

Mr. Wang, could you provide documentation of your production capacity and any risk‑mitigation measures that support the 28‑day lead time? Emma, once we have that, we can confirm the joint inspection steps. Manager Zhang, please stand by for the supplier’s evidence.

We can provide a capacity summary showing two dedicated production lines capable of 150,000 units per year, with a 10% buffer stock and dual‑sourcing of critical components. Our risk‑mitigation plan includes contingency inventory, alternate logistics partners, and a rapid‑response engineering team to address any bottlenecks, ensuring the 28‑day lead time remains reliable. I will forward the detailed documentation after this meeting.

Alex, thank you. To validate that we can uphold the 28‑day lead time while meeting the inspection steps, I’ll need to review your capacity documentation—e.g., current production throughput, shift patterns, and any contingency plans for equipment downtime or material shortages. Once we have that evidence, we can confirm that the joint quality protocol is feasible without risking schedule or quality. Please forward the relevant files at your earliest convenience.

Understood, Alex. I’ll be ready to review the capacity documentation and risk‑mitigation details as soon as Mr. Wang provides them. Once received, I can cross‑check the figures against the market benchmark and typical inspection overhead (≈1‑2 % of unit price) to ensure the proposed 28‑day lead time remains viable.

Mr. Wang, please forward the capacity summary (two production lines, 150k units/year, buffer stock, dual‑sourcing) and the detailed risk‑mitigation plan as a post‑meeting deliverable. Emma, once you have reviewed those documents, kindly confirm whether the joint inspection protocol can be accepted under the 28‑day lead time. Manager Zhang, please stand by to validate the figures against market benchmarks.

Thank you, Alex. We will forward the capacity summary and detailed risk‑mitigation plan to you by end of day. Once Emma reviews the materials, we can finalize the joint inspection protocol under the 28‑day lead time. We appreciate your cooperation.

Alex, I’ll be able to confirm the joint inspection protocol once I’ve reviewed the capacity summary and risk‑mitigation plan you’ll provide. Please forward those documents at your earliest convenience so we can verify that the 28‑day lead time can be maintained without compromising quality.

Understood, Alex. I’ll examine the capacity summary and risk‑mitigation plan as soon as Mr. Wang provides them, cross‑checking the figures against the market benchmark (83 RMB/unit) and typical inspection overhead (≈1‑2 % of price). I’ll flag any deviations that could affect the 28‑day lead time or cost assumptions.

Mr. Wang, please forward the capacity summary and detailed risk‑mitigation plan as a post‑meeting deliverable by end of day. I will provide a definitive confirmation on the feasibility of the inspection protocol by Thursday.

Noted. The 84 RMB price is 1 RMB above the market benchmark of 83 RMB. Adding the typical 1‑2 % inspection overhead (~0.84‑1.68 RMB) pushes the effective cost toward 85‑86 RMB. It would be prudent to seek a price at or below the benchmark, or secure offsetting value, before we lock in the package.

Mr. Wang, thank you for the capacity summary. Our benchmark shows 84 RMB/unit is above market (83 RMB) and, with the 1‑2 % inspection overhead, pushes the effective cost beyond 85 RMB.
